title: Stream pipeline: context propagation and early termination ergonomics for Go SDK
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Problem statement: The current Go SDK stream surface does not make it easy for callers to reliably abort in-flight streams, propagate deadlines to internal goroutines, or observe partial results when an operation is terminated early. This has resulted in customer reports of leaked goroutines during canceled requests, unclear semantics when context deadlines elapse during streaming, and poor ergonomics for common patterns (timeout per-chunk vs overall deadline).

Goal: Rework the streaming implementation and public ergonomics to provide a predictable pipeline model that: 1) reliably propagates cancellation and deadlines to all internal workers; 2) supports early termination with deterministic cleanup; 3) exposes a small set of helpers/examples for common timeouts (per-chunk, overall, and graceful drain); and 4) preserves/respects retry semantics for transient connection errors without violating user deadlines.

Scope: This ticket covers the Go SDK runtime-side changes and API ergonomics (no server changes). Work includes internal pipeline refactor, new helper utilities, unit/integration tests, examples, and docs. It intentionally does not implement resumable checkpointing for disconnected clients — that will be a follow-up.

Non-goals: Changing server-side streaming protocol, adding new top-level API flavors (we keep Recv/RecvChunk style), or introducing a different concurrency model (still goroutine + channels).

Key user scenarios we must be correct for: 1) Caller uses context.WithTimeout for overall request; stream must stop and return ctx.Err() quickly and not leak goroutines. 2) Caller wants to perform short per-chunk timeouts (e.g., wait 200ms for next chunk, otherwise abort) and still observe already-received chunks. 3) Network flaps cause a transient transport error: client should attempt limited reconnect/retry but not extend user deadline. 4) Caller cancels due to UI action: SDK should best-effort flush buffered chunks and close underlying connection gracefully.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover cancellation propagation: canceling parent context aborts all internal goroutines within 50ms in CI
Integration test demonstrating per-chunk timeout pattern via helper (example in examples/stream_timeout)
No goroutine leaks in stress test (1000 concurrent short-lived streams) for 2 minutes
SDK sample docs updated with three patterns: overall deadline, per-chunk deadline, graceful drain
Benchmarks show <5% regressive latency for happy-path streaming vs current main branch
PR is reviewed and signed off by 2 SDK maintainers and one runtime engineer
design_notes: New internal abstraction: streamPipeline which wires three goroutines: transport reader, dispatcher, and aggregator. All goroutines accept ctx and select on ctx.Done() for immediate termination.

Transport reader will attach deadlines using ctx.Deadline() where available and will short-circuit reads that exceed per-read deadlines. We will keep a separate perChunkTimeout helper that wraps the aggregator's Recv loop (no implicit global change).
Add a 'CancelableBuffer' (ring buffer) that supports DrainWithTimeout(ctx, timeout) so callers can request graceful flush on cancel while bounding how long flush can take.

Retry behavior: network retries are performed by the transport reader only and are bounded by remaining time until parent ctx deadline. Retries will not create new root contexts; they reuse the same ctx to prevent deadline extension.

API ergonomics: keep existing Stream.Recv() signature but add Stream.WithPerChunkTimeout(d time.Duration) builder and convenience function streamutil.ReadAllWithTimeout(ctx, stream, perChunkTimeout). Examples will be provided in examples/ directory.
Trade-offs: keeping Recv() signature preserves backward compatibility but requires additional helpers rather than fundamental API change. This minimizes churn for customers.

Observability: emit an event on cancellation path (sdk.stream.cancelled) with labels: reason=deadline|user_cancel|signal, duration_ms, goroutine_count_snapshot. Hook into existing console telemetry pipeline but default sampling low to avoid noise.
